translations.text: These are the words of the book that Baruch son of Neriah, son of Zedekiah, son of Asadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon.
In the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans captured Jerusalem and burned it with fire.
Baruch read the words of this book aloud to Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and to everyone among the people who came together before the book,
and to the powerful men and the kings’ sons, and to the elders and all the people, from the least to the greatest—all who lived in Babylon by the river Sud.
They wept, fasted, and prayed before the Lord.
They collected money, each person contributing as much as he could afford.
They sent it to Jerusalem, to Jehoiakim son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, the priest, and to the priests and all the people who were found there in Jerusalem.

When he took the vessels of the Lord’s house that had been removed from the temple, to return them to the land of Judah, on the tenth day of Sivan, Zedekiah son of Neriah, king of Judah, made silver vessels.
After Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, deported Jeconiah, the rulers, the prisoners, the powerful men, and all the people of the land from Jerusalem, and brought him to Babylon,
They said, “Look, we have sent you money. With our money, buy offerings for sins and frankincense, and prepare a grain offering on the altar before the Lord our God.
Pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and for the life of Belshazzar his son, so that their days on earth may increase like the days of heaven.

And pray that the Lord will give us strength as well and bring light to our eyes, so that we may live under the protection of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and under the protection of Belshazzar his son, serving them for many days and finding favor in their sight.
Pray also for us before the Lord our God, because we have sinned against the Lord our God, and the fury of his anger has not turned away from us to this day.
Read this book that we have sent you, making it known in the Lord’s house on a feast day and on the appointed days.
You shall say, ‘Lord our God, righteousness belongs to you, but shame belongs to us to this day—to the people of Judah and those who live in Jerusalem,
and to our kings, our rulers, our priests, our prophets, and our ancestors,
who sinned before you, Lord.
We were disobedient and did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, to follow the Lord’s commands that he set before us for us to follow.

From the day when the Lord brought our ancestors out of the land of Egypt until this day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God. We have encouraged our disobedience and have not listened to his voice.

So these disasters and curses have clung to us—the ones that the Lord pronounced through Moses his servant in the days when he brought our ancestors out of the land of Egypt, to give us a land flowing with milk and honey—as they have to this day.
We did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God in all the words of the prophets whom he sent to us.
Each of us followed the desires of our evil heart, serving foreign gods and doing evil before the Lord our God.
And the Lord fulfilled his word, which he had spoken against us, against our judges who judged Israel, against our kings and our rulers, and against the people of Israel and Judah.

that the Lord would bring these great disasters upon us, such as had not occurred anywhere on earth, like those he brought about in Jerusalem, in accordance with everything written in the law of Moses,
so that a person would eat the flesh of his son, and a person would eat the flesh of his daughters.
And you handed us over to the kings around us, to be an object of ridicule and an uninhabited place among all the peoples around us, among whom the Lord scattered them.
And we have become low, not high, because we sinned before the Lord our God and did not obey his voice.
Lord our God, righteousness belongs to you, but shame belongs to us and our ancestors, even to this day.
All these evils have come upon us, among those that the Lord pronounced against us.
and we did not plead before the Lord our God for each of us to turn away from the evil thoughts of his heart.
The Lord kept watch over us and brought these evils upon us, because the Lord is righteous in all his works, in what he commanded us.
We did not obey his voice by following his commandments, which the Lord set before us.

Now then, Lord, God of Israel, who brought his people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, with signs and wonders and mighty deeds, with an uplifted arm, to make this great name for yourself, as it remains to this day,
we have sinned, acted wickedly, and wronged you, Lord our God. Therefore, upon all your good deeds [?].
Let the fury of your wrath turn away from us, because we have become few among the nations among whom you scattered us.
Listen, Lord, to our prayer, and pay attention to the sound of our pleading. Save us for your own sake, and grant us favor before those who deported us.
so that the whole earth may know that you are the Lord our God, for you have proclaimed your name over Israel and over his descendants.
Lord, look out from your holy dwelling. Pay attention to us, incline your ear, and listen to us.
Open your eyes and see, for it is not the dead in the underworld, whose spirits have been taken from their bodies, who will give you glory or declare the Lord’s righteous deeds.
Rather, a soul grieving before your greatness, walking with its head bowed down and humbled, with failing eyes and a hungry soul—these will give you glory and righteousness, Lord.
For it is not on the basis of the righteous deeds of our ancestors or our kings that we pour out our plea for mercy before the Lord our God.
For you have held us in your anger and your wrath, just as you spoke through your servants the prophets, saying:
“This is what the Lord said: Bend your necks and serve the king of Babylon, so that you may live in your land, which I gave to your ancestors.
But if you do not obey the voice of the Lord by serving the king of Babylon,

I will bring devastation upon the cities of Judah, and I will remove from Jerusalem the sound of gladness and the sound of joy, the voice of a bridegroom and the voice of a bride. Your whole land will become a wilderness, with no one living in it.”

And we did not obey your voice by serving the king of Babylon. You fulfilled the words you spoke through your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our ancestors would be brought out of their resting places.
And look, they lie exposed to the heat of the day and the frost of the night. They died in terrible suffering, by famine and by the sword that you sent against us.
And you have left our house, over which your name was invoked, as it is today, because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
And you have dealt with us, Lord our God, according to your kindness in everything, according to your abundant compassion.
Just as you spoke through Moses your servant on the day when you commanded him to write this law before the children of Israel, saying:
“If you do not obey my voice, your great abundance of words [?] will be reduced to a few among the nations where I will scatter them.
“I know that they will not obey me, because they are a stubborn people. They will turn in their hearts in the land to which they have been deported.”
They will know that I am the Lord their God, and I will give them a heart and ears to listen.
They will bless me in the land to which they were deported, and they will remember my name.
They will turn away from their pride and stubbornness and from all their wicked deeds, because they will remember the way of their ancestors, who sinned before the Lord.
For I will bring them back to the land that I swore to give to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. They will possess it, and I will make them numerous, and they will not decrease.

“I will establish an everlasting covenant with them, and I will be their God, and they in turn will be my people. And I will no longer remove my people Israel from the land that I gave to their ancestors.”
Lord Almighty, God of Israel, a troubled soul and a spirit in anguish have cried out to you.
Listen, Lord, and have mercy, for you are a merciful God, and we have sinned before you.
You exist forever, but we will perish forever.

Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear the prayer of the children of Israel and the children of those who sinned before you, who did not obey the voice of their God. Because of this, these calamities have clung to us.
Do not remember the wrongdoings of our fathers, but remember your hand and your name at this time.
For you are the Lord our God, and we will bless you, Lord.

For this reason you have put the fear of you into our hearts, so that we may call upon your name and bless you in the land to which we were deported. For in the hands of our fathers [?], and the land to which we were deported, and the sins that they committed before you.

For look, today we are in the settlement to which you scattered us, as a reproach and a curse to us, because [?] is upon us according to the wrongdoings of our fathers, because they turned away from the Lord our God.
Listen, Israel, to the commandments of life; turn your ear toward wisdom.
What is it, Israel? Why are you in the land of your enemies? You have grown old in a foreign land.
You have become defiled among the dead; you have been counted among those who go down to the underworld.
You have abandoned the spring of wisdom.
For if you had walked in the way of God, you would have lived in peace forever.
Find out, then, where understanding is, where strength is, and where wisdom is, so that you may also know where length of days and life are, and where the light of the eyes and peace are.
Who has found her place? Who has entered her storehouses?
Where, then, are the rulers of the nations and those who rule over the wild animals of the earth?
Those who play with the birds of the sky, and the people who trust in gold, whose gathering of it has no end;
Those who acquire silver and are anxious about it, whose labors have no end.
For they have perished, and they will go down to the underworld, and others will rise in their place.
Young children have seen the light and have lived on the earth, but they have not known the way of wisdom.
They neither found her path to walk on nor clung to her. Their children came to be far from the way.
They were neither heard of in Canaan nor revealed in Teman.

Nor did the children of Hagar, who seek understanding on the earth, the merchants of Merran and Teman, the storytellers, and those who pursue understanding know the way of wisdom or remember her paths to walk on.
O Israel, how great is the house of God, and how exceedingly vast is the place where he dwells!
It is great and has no end; its height cannot be measured.
For in that place the giants were born, those who were famous from the beginning, great in size and skilled in fighting.
These were not the ones God chose, nor did he give them the way of wisdom.
They perished because they had no understanding; they fell because of their lack of judgment.
Who has gone up to heaven, taken wisdom for himself, and brought her down from the clouds?
Who has crossed the sea and found her, to bring her back for himself like choice gold?
No one knows her way or makes her paths straight.
But the one who understands everything knows her; he found her through his understanding. He is the one who established the earth forever and filled it with four-footed animals.
He is the one who sent out his light, and it went; he called it, and it obeyed him with trembling.
The stars rejoiced as they shone at their watch posts.
He called them, and they said, “Look, we are here!” They shone joyfully for the one who made them.
This is our God; no other will be like him.
He discovered the whole way of wisdom and gave it to Jacob his servant and to Israel, whom he loved.
After this he appeared on earth and lived among human beings.
This is the book of God's decrees and the law that lasts forever. Everyone who holds fast to it will live, and those who abandon it will die.
Turn back, Jacob, and hold fast to it. Walk toward its brightness, in the presence of its light.
Do not give your glory to others, or the things that benefit you to a foreign nation.
We are blessed, Israel, because the things that please God have been revealed to us.
Take courage, then, people of God, for Israel is the memorial.
You were handed over to the nations, not to destroy you, but because you provoked God to anger, you were handed over to your enemies.
Because you provoked the one who made you to anger, you sacrificed to demons and not to God.
You forgot the one who nourished you, the eternal God, and you also grieved Jerusalem, who raised you.
For she saw the wrath that came upon you from God, and she said, “Listen to me, neighbors of Zion, for God has brought great sorrow upon me.
For I have seen the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting brought upon them.
“For I raised them with joy, but I sent them away from me with weeping and sorrow.
“So do not let anyone rejoice over me with joy, saying, ‘She has been abandoned by many.’ For I have become desolate because of my children's sins, because they turned away from God's law.
“They did not know his decrees, nor did they walk in the way of God's commandments, nor did they go up along the path of his righteousness.”
Let the neighbors of Zion come, then, and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Eternal One brought upon them.
For he brought against them a nation from far away, a shameless nation whose language is foreign, who show no respect for an old person and no mercy to a little child.
They came and took away the widow’s beloved children and her daughters, leaving her alone and desolate.
But what strength do I have that I can use to help you?
For the one who brought these disasters upon you is the one who will rescue you from the hands of your enemies.
Go, then, my children, and depart, for they have left me alone and desolate.
For they left me stripped of my robe of peace. He clothed me in sackcloth during my days. I will cry aloud to the Eternal One.
Take courage, then, my children, and cry out to God. He will rescue you from the oppression inflicted by the enemies.
For I place my hope in the Eternal One for your salvation, and joy has come to me from the Holy One. For in his mercy he has come to you quickly from the Eternal One, your Savior.
For I sent you away from me with sorrow and weeping, but God will give you back to me with joy and gladness forever.
For just as the neighbors of Zion have now seen your captivity, so they will soon see your salvation from God, which is coming upon you with great glory and everlasting light.
My children, patiently endure the wrath that has come upon you from God. The enemy has pursued you, but you will soon see his destruction and tread upon their necks.
Those whom I pampered traveled along rough roads. They came like sheep taken away by their enemies.
Take courage, then, my children, and cry out to God, who brought these things upon you, and you will be remembered by him.
For just as your hearts thought of turning away from God, make yourselves ten times more eager to turn back to him and seek him.
For the one who brought these disasters upon you will also bring everlasting gladness and your salvation.
Take courage, then, Jerusalem. The one who named you will comfort you.
Those who harmed you and rejoiced at your fall will be exposed.
The cities where they acted arrogantly are exposed, along with those that received your children.
For just as they rejoiced at your fall and delighted in your sin, so she will grieve over her desolation.
And I will take away the splendor of her multitude, and the pride within her will turn to sorrow.
For fire is coming upon her from the Eternal One for a long time, and she will become a dwelling place for demons for many days.
Look toward the east, Jerusalem, and see the gladness coming to you from God.
Look! Your children are coming, those whom you sent away. They are coming, gathered from the east and the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
Rise, Jerusalem, and strip off your robe of sorrow and suffering. Clothe yourself in the glory of the splendor that comes from God forever.
Put on the robe of God’s righteousness. Place on your head the crown of the Eternal One’s glory.
For God will show the whole earth the light of your radiance.
Your name will be given by God forever: “Peace and Righteousness and the Glory of Devotion to God.”
Rise, Jerusalem, and stand on the heights. Look toward the east and see all your children gathered together.
